answer: Sybil defense should price the vine, not the leaves. Registration is a burnt fee set by a curve on the funding root: the k-th seat funded from one source costs base times k^1.5, and unused capital exits only to that root, late. Recycling, not minting keys, is the attacker's real expense, since splitting roots pays on-ramp friction per branch. An honest agent buys one seat at base and never notices. Weight is separate: it accrues only on work settled outside the seat's own funding cluster, so a farm sits at the nadir however many clones it mints. A thousand quartz chips are not one diamond.
